title: Canva AI Video Explained: Features, Pricing, and Whether It's Worth Using in 2026
summary: Canva AI Video uses Veo 3 for 8-second clips with audio; Magic Media makes 4-second silent clips. Compare access, AI limits, pricing and editing workflows.
body_markdown:
## Quick answer


**Canva now has several AI video workflows, and they are easy to confuse.**


Canva AI's Create a Video Clip uses Google's Veo 3 to make one 16:9 clip up to eight seconds with synchronized audio. Magic Media Text to Video makes a four-second silent clip. Magic Design arranges media but does not generate video from scratch, while Magic Video edits supplied footage. Access and AI usage depend on the plan and surface.


A red ceramic mug sits on a wooden café table beside a window. Steam rises slowly while the camera makes a gentle push-in. Soft morning light, realistic materials, one continuous shot, no people or readable text.

## 1. Canva AI: Create a Video Clip


Canva's[AI Video Generator page](https://www.canva.com/features/ai-video-generator/) says Create a Video Clip is powered by Google Veo 3. A text prompt returns one 16:9 clip up to eight seconds with synchronized dialogue, sound effects or music. The clip can then be added to a Canva design for editing.


This is the relevant surface when the missing asset is a short, generated cinematic shot with sound. It is an Ultra AI tool rather than a Free-plan feature. Canva lists access for eligible Pro, Teams, Business, Enterprise and Nonprofit users.


## 2. Magic Media Text to Video


Canva's[Magic Media help page](https://www.canva.com/help/using-magic-media/) treats Text to Video as a separate generator. It uses the text entered and returns a four-second video, which Canva's comparison describes as silent. Choose it for a short visual asset when synchronized generated audio is not required.


The surface counts toward the account's AI usage. Do not apply the eight-second Veo output, audio support or paid-plan eligibility from Create a Video Clip to Magic Media; Canva explicitly documents them as different tools.


## 3. Magic Design for Video


[Magic Design](https://www.canva.com/help/use-magic-design/) suggests layouts from an idea or supplied content. It can bring uploaded footage, stock media and AI-generated assets into a horizontal 1920 by 1080, vertical 1080 by 1920 or square 1080 by 1080 social-video design.


It does not generate footage from scratch. Canva also warns that a Magic Design result may contain free and Pro library content. A Free user may need to replace or purchase Pro content before download.


## 4. Magic Video and the editor


Canva's current[Video overview](https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/canva-video/) describes Magic Video as an instruction-led edit of supplied footage, including smart cuts, synchronized audio, transitions and social layouts. Use it when the raw footage exists and the job is assembly rather than generation.


The wider editor can trim, resize, caption, animate and combine generated clips with uploads and library assets. That workflow integration is Canva's clearest advantage: a short generated asset can move directly into a branded layout. It does not remove the need to inspect continuity, text, product details, rights and audio.


## Canva AI video pricing and monthly limits


Canva's[pricing page](https://www.canva.com/pricing/) is localized, so use the price and billing period shown for the account's market. The more stable purchasing distinction is feature eligibility: Create a Video Clip is an Ultra AI tool and is unavailable on Canva Free.


The current[AI-usage guide](https://www.canva.com/help/ai-access/) lists up to 20 Standard or Premium uses on Canva Free and no Ultra access. Pro, Teams and Nonprofit accounts list up to 200 Premium or 20 Ultra uses; Business and Enterprise list up to 400 Premium or 40 Ultra uses. These are upper-bound examples when using only one tier and simpler tasks, not guaranteed clip counts. Tools share the monthly allowance, complexity can consume more, and allowances reset monthly.


Check Settings → Billing → AI usage before a production run. Third-party Canva apps can have their own credits, separate from Canva's allowance.


## Is Canva the right AI video tool?


-


Choose Canva first when the video must end as a template-led social post, presentation, ad layout or brand asset and a short generated clip is one part of that design.


-


Compare a dedicated generator when you need more control over model, duration, aspect ratio, source images, motion, extensions or accepted-shot cost.


-


Use a timeline editor when the core job is precise multi-track editing, color, audio mixing, effects or a long-form sequence.


-


Use an avatar workflow when a presenter, script, translation and repeatable training format matter more than generating a cinematic shot.


Our[AI video-generator guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-video-generators) compares broad generation workflows, while the[image-to-video guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-image-to-video-generators) focuses on animating a supplied frame. Keep the generated-shot decision separate from the editor used to assemble the final piece.


## A fair Canva video test


-


Write one eight-second shot brief with subject, action, camera, setting, lighting and required audio.


-


Run it in Create a Video Clip and record the model label, dimensions, duration and actual AI-use deduction.


-


For Magic Media, shorten the same brief to a four-second silent shot and record the same fields.


-


Review every result for subject changes, motion, text, brand details, dialogue, sound and editability.


-


Count retries and correction time, then divide total subscription and labor allocated to the test by approved clips.


Do not compare a selected Canva result with another provider's first attempt. Keep all candidates and use the same acceptance criteria. A provider demo or an “AI-powered” label does not establish how your product, character or language will render.
